svg.title: The lowest GLP-1 doses ever tested in randomized trials, and what they did to weight
svg.desc: Semaglutide once-daily phase 2 trial, 957 adults with obesity, weight change at 52 weeks: Placebo -2.3%, 0.05 mg/day -6.0%, 0.1 mg/day -8.6%, 0.2 mg/day -11.6%, 0.3 mg/day -11.2%, 0.4 mg/day -13.8%. Tirzepatide phase 2 trial, 318 adults with type 2 diabetes, weight change at 26 weeks: Placebo -0.4 kg, 1 mg/week -0.9 kg, 5 mg/week -4.8 kg, 10 mg/week -8.7 kg, 15 mg/week -11.3 kg. The lowest semaglutide dose still beat placebo; 1 mg of tirzepatide barely moved weight.

text.font-family: Inter, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Tiny doses have been tested. They did not all work.

svg.text: Read across with care: different drugs, people, units and trial lengths; daily semaglutide was never marketed.

text.font-family: Inter, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Tirzepatide 1 mg sits inside the usual “microdose” range (25–50% of the 2.5 mg starter dose). It cut HbA1c by 1.06

text.font-family: Inter, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: points (placebo 0.06) and caused stomach side effects in 23.1% (placebo 9.8%). Semaglutide “microdoses” (25–50%

text.font-family: Inter, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: of 0.25 mg, about 0.06–0.13 mg a week) are below any dose tested for weight in a randomized trial.
